source: Microsoft Excel financial functions reference (support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/financial-functions-reference), fetched 2026-07-11

entries.name: ACCRINT
entries.description: Returns the accrued interest for a security that pays periodic interest
entries.repr: date-composition (extends calendrical-checksum) + checked-int arithmetic for the accrual formula
entries.reason: ACCRINT's signature is all scalars (issue, first_interest, settlement dates; rate; par; frequency; basis code 0-4) so it doesn't trip the array-state-field gap, and the accrual itself (par*rate*accrued_fraction, summed by frequency) is plain checked multiply/divide, not a transcendental — so it isn't host_only. But it fundamentally depends on day-count BASIS conventions (30/360 US, 30/360 European, actual/actual, actual/360, actual/365), and cell80 has none of those today: calendrical-checksum only ships raw calendar-day primitives (days_between, day_of_year, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date, day_of_week, is_weekday, is_weekend per docs/cell-index.md) with no basis-adjusted day-count logic and no coupon-period/frequency schedule handling. That's real new algorithmic content (multi-step case analysis per basis code, not one or two existing outputs glued together), so per docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 4's IRR/RATE precedent this is a composable-disguise misclassification risk if filed as composable-author — it belongs in candidate, gated on first landing day-count-convention cells (e.g. days_360_us, days_360_eu, day_count_act_act, day_count_act_360, day_count_act_365) as prerequisites, then ACCRINT itself as a coupon-frequency loop over one of those.

entries.name: ACCRINTM
entries.description: Returns the accrued interest for a security that pays interest at maturity
entries.repr: date-composition
entries.reason: ACCRINTM = par * rate * YEARFRAC(issue, settlement, basis), where basis selects one of Excel's five day-count conventions (30/360 US, actual/actual, actual/360, actual/365, 30/360 European). cell80's calendrical-checksum pack has the calendar primitives (days_between, day_of_year, is_leap_year, days_in_month, is_valid_date) and checked-arithmetic has the final multiply (mul3_checked_u32 fits par*rate*fraction shape), but no cell anywhere computes a day-count-convention year-fraction — 30/360's day-of-month clamping and actual/actual's period-straddling logic don't exist as cells today, per docs/cell-index.md. Per docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md this is a function that fundamentally depends on an unbuilt day-count convention, not just a calendar day-difference, so it isn't glue-composable from what's shipped — it's real new logic (a bounded 5-way case split over existing date primitives), not host_only (no transcendental, no array-state need: issue/settlement/rate/par/basis are all scalar fields). Target: a date-composition tier day-count/year-fraction cell (or family, one per basis) as the real prerequisite, with ACCRINTM's own multiply riding on mul3_checked_u32/mul_checked_u32 once that fraction exists.

entries.name: AMORDEGRC
entries.description: Returns the depreciation for each accounting period by using a depreciation coefficient
entries.repr: date-composition (plus checked-int/bps-style fixed point for the coefficient table and depreciation loop)
entries.reason: No depreciation or day-count-convention cells exist in cell80 today (docs/cell-index.md has calendrical primitives like day_of_year/days_between/is_leap_year/is_valid_date but nothing implementing a basis convention like 30/360 or actual/actual, and no finance/depreciation pack exists at all in cell80/cells/*). AMORDEGRC needs (1) a rate-to-coefficient lookup table, (2) a prorated first-period fraction computed under an explicit day-count basis (0=360 NASD, 1=actual, 3=365, 4=European 30/360) — genuinely missing prerequisite logic, not just calendar-day differencing — and (3) an iterative per-period depreciation loop with a remaining-value floor and a distinct last-period rule. This is real multi-branch algorithmic complexity, not glue of 1-2 existing cells, so per the taxonomy note's own IRR/RATE worked example it should be filed as candidate rather than composable-author. It is not host_only: no transcendentals are needed (the loop is repeated multiplication, same idiom as compound_decrease_by_bps/frac_pow) and every input (cost, date_purchased, first_period, salvage, period, rate, basis) is a fixed scalar, so the array-state-field harness gap doesn't apply.

entries.name: AMORLINC
entries.description: Returns the depreciation for each accounting period
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: days_between, day_of_year, days_in_month, is_leap_year (existing date primitives it would build from — none of them encode a day-count convention)
entries.repr: date-composition (day-count-fraction prerequisite) + checked-int (period-stepping depreciation math)
entries.reason: AMORLINC computes French straight-line depreciation per period from (cost, date_purchased, first_period, salvage, period, rate, basis), where the first period is prorated by a day-count FRACTION selected by `basis` (0=30/360 US, 1=actual/actual, 2=actual/360, 3=actual/365, 4=30/360 EU) and the final period is capped so cumulative depreciation never exceeds cost-salvage. cell80 has calendar-day primitives (`days_between`, `day_of_year`, `days_in_month`, `is_leap_year`, `is_valid_date` in calendrical-checksum) but no day-count-CONVENTION cell — 30/360 and actual/360/365 fractions are a distinct, unbuilt calculation, not just a calendar day difference. That prerequisite gap plus the multi-step case analysis (distinguish first/middle/last period, cap at salvage, thread cumulative depreciation across period calls the way rate_window_update/sliding_window_counter_step already thread state) is genuine algorithmic complexity, not one- or two-cell glue, so it fails composable-author's own reason-2 sanity check and belongs in candidate. It is not host_only: no transcendental is needed (straight-line, just cost*rate arithmetic) and no arbitrary-length array input is needed (all inputs are fixed scalars), so neither of the two harness gaps applies here.

entries.name: COUPDAYBS
entries.description: Returns the number of days from the beginning of the coupon period to the settlement date
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: Prerequisites only (none sufficient alone): is_leap_year, days_in_month, is_valid_date, days_between — cell80/cells/calendrical-checksum/
entries.repr: date-composition
entries.reason: No coupon/settlement/maturity/frequency/basis cell exists in docs/cell-index.md. COUPDAYBS needs two pieces of genuinely new logic: (1) a previous-coupon-date calculator that steps back from maturity by 12/frequency-month increments with month-end anchoring, and (2) day-count basis-convention counting (30/360 US/EU vs actual/360/365/actual) applied to settlement minus that PCD — the 30/360 bases are not raw calendar-day differences, so days_between alone doesn't cover it. This is new date logic, not glue of 1-2 existing outputs, so per the taxonomy's own reason-2 self-check it belongs in candidate rather than composable-author.

entries.name: COUPDAYS
entries.description: Returns the number of days in the coupon period that contains the settlement date
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: none — nearest existing primitives are days_between, day_of_year, days_in_month, is_leap_year (all in calendrical-checksum), none of which perform coupon-schedule-date location or day-count-basis dispatch
entries.repr: date-composition (checked-int day-count arithmetic on y/m/d state fields)
entries.reason: No coupon/bond/day-count-basis cell exists anywhere in the library (grepped docs/cell-index.md for coup/bond/frequency/basis — nothing; calendrical-checksum's day_of_week/day_of_year/days_between/days_in_month/is_leap_year/is_valid_date are the only date primitives shipped). COUPDAYS looks superficially composable from those, but it actually needs two pieces of new logic none of them provide: (1) locating the coupon period that contains settlement — the previous/next coupon date anchored to maturity's month/day stepped by 12/frequency months, a schedule-finding routine none of days_between/day_of_year do; and (2) a basis-conditional dispatch (Excel's basis 0/2/4 return a fixed 360/frequency or lookup, but basis=1, actual/actual, requires the real day-count of that specific coupon period, which can vary with leap years). Per the taxonomy amendment's own guidance (Part 2 reason 2, and the worked IRR/RATE example), a case needing genuine new algorithmic logic like this — not glue of 1-2 existing outputs — belongs in candidate, not composable-author.

entries.name: COUPDAYSNC
entries.description: Returns the number of days from the settlement date to the next coupon date
entries.repr: date-composition (state-cell with year/month/day fields) + checked-int arithmetic for the day-count formula — no floats or transcendentals needed
entries.reason: Not composable from today's calendrical-checksum pack (day_of_week, day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date, is_weekday, is_weekend, per docs/cell-index.md) — every one of those operates on a single already-known date or a pair of already-known dates; none locates a coupon date by stepping backward from maturity in frequency-sized month increments (with end-of-month clamping), which is what "next coupon date" fundamentally requires, and none implement a 30/360-style day-count (US or European) as opposed to actual-calendar Rata-Die subtraction. COUPDAYSNC needs two genuinely new pieces of logic: (1) a coupon-schedule search — month-stepping from maturity back toward settlement, bracketing it between two coupon dates — and (2) a basis-dispatch day-count (basis 0/2/3 use actual days akin to days_between; basis 0 US 30/360 and basis 4 European 30/360 need distinct month/day-clamp formulas days_between doesn't do). This is real new algorithmic work, not glue over 1-2 existing cells, so per docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 2 reason 2's caveat it belongs in candidate rather than composable-author. It's not host_only: no transcendentals and no array-state fields are needed (settlement, maturity, frequency, basis are all fixed scalar/state-cell fields), matching the doc's guidance that day-count-convention gaps are real prerequisite work for candidate, not automatically host_only.

entries.name: COUPNCD
entries.description: Returns the next coupon date after the settlement date
entries.repr: date-composition
entries.reason: No coupon/bond pack exists in docs/cell-index.md at all yet (grep for coup/bond/maturity/frequency/settlement returns nothing) — only the calendrical-checksum pack exists (day_of_week, day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date, is_weekday, is_weekend), and none of those do date-schedule arithmetic. COUPNCD's actual algorithm is: step the maturity date backward in whole 12/frequency-month increments (with end-of-month/leap-year clamping that differs by day-count basis) until finding the first coupon date strictly after settlement — that's month-add-to-date plus a bounded search loop, a genuinely new primitive none of the existing days_between/day_of_year/is_valid_date cells provide (they only diff or validate calendar dates, none step a date by N months). This isn't glue over 1-2 existing cells, so it fails composable on reason 2's own check (real algorithmic complexity belongs in candidate, not composable-author). It's also not host_only: inputs are a fixed small set of scalars (settlement y/m/d, maturity y/m/d, frequency, basis — 8 u16 fields), no array/variable-length schedule and no transcendental math, just checked-int date-composition logic plus a bounded loop (same idiom class as frac_pow's repeated-multiply escalation). Worth flagging: this "add N months with EOM/basis clamping" primitive would be the shared foundation for the whole COUP* family (COUPPCD, COUPDAYS, COUPDAYBS, COUPDAYSNC, COUPNUM), so it's a good first candidate to unlock that cluster rather than a one-off.

entries.name: COUPNUM
entries.description: Returns the number of coupons payable between the settlement date and maturity date
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: calendrical-checksum: day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date (adjacent primitives, none sufficient -- month-stepping/coupon-schedule-date generation is missing)
entries.repr: date-composition
entries.reason: COUPNUM counts coupon dates by stepping backward from maturity in fixed steps of 12/frequency months (freq in {1,2,4}) until stepping past settlement, which needs month-level date arithmetic (add/subtract N months to a date, with end-of-month clamping, e.g. Jan 31 -> Feb 28/29) that no existing cell provides. calendrical-checksum's day_of_week/day_of_year/days_between/days_in_month/is_leap_year/is_valid_date (docs/cell-index.md) give day-granularity primitives -- calendar validity, day counts, day-of-week -- but nothing composes a month-stepped coupon schedule from them; days_between only diffs two already-known dates, it doesn't generate the intermediate anchor dates COUPNUM needs. All inputs are small fixed scalars (settlement y/m/d, maturity y/m/d, frequency, basis code), so this isn't blocked by array-state fields or transcendentals -- it needs a new bounded counting loop over a new month-roll primitive, which is genuine new date-composition logic rather than glue over existing cells.

entries.name: COUPPCD
entries.description: Returns the previous coupon date before the settlement date
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: none existing — nearest relatives are calendrical-checksum's days_in_month/is_leap_year/is_valid_date (day-length/validity only, no month-add/subtract) and days_between (year-spanning serial-day diff, but whole-date-to-whole-date, not month-stepped)
entries.repr: date-composition
entries.reason: docs/cell-index.md's calendrical-checksum pack (day_of_week, day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date, is_weekday, is_weekend) has no month-stepping primitive at all — nothing subtracts N months from a (year,month,day) with day-of-month clamping across variable month lengths and year boundaries. COUPPCD's actual algorithm (Excel's basis argument doesn't change the date math, only later day-count functions) is: anchor at maturity, step backward in (12/frequency)-month increments, clamped to end-of-month, until landing on the coupon date just before settlement. That's a genuinely new date primitive plus a bounded backward-search loop over it, not glue over existing cells, so it isn't composable-skip/author -- it needs new logic to exist first (this is exactly the misclassification check docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 2 reason 2 flags: real complexity here means candidate, not composable). No transcendental math and no array-state-field dependency (fixed scalar arity: settlement, maturity, frequency, basis), so it is not host_only.

entries.name: CUMIPMT
entries.description: Returns the cumulative interest paid between two periods
entries.repr: checked-int (money-bps style: bps rate + wide u32 balance/payment fields, following compound_increase_by_bps/compound_decrease_by_bps precedent) with f32 as a fallback tier if bps granularity (0.01%) proves too coarse for real loan rates
entries.reason: No PMT/IPMT/amortization cell exists anywhere in docs/cell-index.md — the nearest existing pieces are money-bps's compound_increase_by_bps/compound_decrease_by_bps (loop a single bps rate over `periods`, but with no principal repayment/declining balance) and fractions/frac_pow (the repeated-multiply (n/d)^k idiom). CUMIPMT needs (1+rate)^nper compounding to derive the fixed payment, then a bounded per-period loop tracking outstanding balance to sum interest across [start_period, end_period] — genuine algorithmic complexity (taxonomy reason 2), not 1-2-cell glue, so it fails composable-anything on its own terms and its natural prerequisite (a PMT/IPMT-equivalent) isn't shipped either. Not host_only: nper/start_period/end_period are small bounded integer loop bounds (not a transcendental — same idiom as frac_pow/compound_increase_by_bps), all inputs are fixed small-arity scalars (rate, nper, pv, start_period, end_period, type), and no date/day-count convention is involved (periods are integers, not calendar dates).

entries.name: CUMPRINC
entries.description: Returns the cumulative principal paid on a loan between two periods
entries.reason: No existing cell covers or composes this: docs/cell-index.md has no PMT/IPMT/PPMT/CUMIPMT/annuity/amortization cell anywhere (grepped the full index), and the closest analogues — money-bps's compound_increase_by_bps/compound_decrease_by_bps (apply one fixed rate for N periods, no per-period principal/interest split or partial-range accumulation) and fractions' frac_pow (bounded repeated-multiply power, same idiom needed here) — only supply the compounding sub-primitive, not the function. CUMPRINC needs (1) an annuity-payment formula pmt = rate*pv/(1-(1+rate)^-nper), itself a bounded power loop like frac_pow/pow_checked_u32 but in f32 since rate/pv are real-valued, then (2) a second bounded loop from start_period to end_period tracking a running balance, computing interest = balance*rate and principal = pmt - interest each step, and accumulating principal into the answer, with a type flag adjusting the first period for annuity-due. That is two chained non-trivial loops with running state, not glue over 1-2 existing outputs — per the taxonomy note's own guidance (Part 4, the IRR/RATE row), when 'genuine complexity' is the only applicable composable-author reason it usually signals the row belongs in candidate instead, which is the case here. None of the three named host_only blockers actually apply: rate/nper/pv/start_period/end_period/type are all scalars (no arbitrary-length cash-flow array, so the array-state-field gap doesn't bite), the only power involved is an integer exponent (nper periods), not a transcendental, and periods here are discrete loan-period counts, not calendar dates, so no day-count convention is implicated.

entries.name: DB
entries.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset for a specified period by using the fixed-declining balance method
entries.reason: No existing cell covers fixed-declining-balance depreciation — grep of docs/cell-index.md finds only compound_decrease_by_bps (money-bps, a fixed KNOWN-bps repeated-decrease loop) and bps_rate_over_2_periods (an Nth-root recovery, but hardcoded to N=2 via isqrt) — no general Nth-root/fractional-power cell and no depreciation-specific cell exist. DB's own formula genuinely needs: (1) rate = 1-(salvage/cost)^(1/life) rounded to 3dp — solvable without a transcendental by Newton-iterating x^life=ratio (all-integer powers + derivative, same shape as RATE/IRR's Newton loop, so not host_only on transcendental grounds), (2) a first-period pro-ration by month/12, (3) a bounded per-period compounding loop shaped like compound_decrease_by_bps's but real-valued and returning only the requested period's delta rather than the final cumulative value, and (4) an optional stub last-period case prorated by (12-month)/12. That's multiple new algorithmic pieces plus case analysis and a convergence loop, not 1-2-cell glue — per the taxonomy note's own worked example for IRR/RATE ("nominally composable but really an algorithm... file as candidate, not composable-author"), this belongs in candidate. Inputs (cost, salvage, life, period, month) are all scalars, so no array-state-field or day-count-convention gap applies here.

entries.name: DDB
entries.description: Calculates depreciation using the double-declining balance method or alternative approaches
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: closest existing cell: compound_decrease_by_bps (money-bps pack) — supplies the iterate-N-periods-over-a-rate loop shape but lacks DDB's per-period min(book_value*rate, book_value-salvage) floor and early-halt-at-salvage logic
entries.repr: checked-int (bps-rate loop, extending the money-bps pack idiom); f32 is a plausible alternate tier
entries.reason: No existing cell covers DDB, and it is not simple glue of 1-2 cells: it needs rate = factor/life, then a bounded loop from period 1 up to the target period tracking book_value, where each step computes depreciation = min(book_value*rate, book_value - salvage) and halts early once book_value hits salvage. compound_decrease_by_bps (money-bps pack) is the closest existing cell — same iterate-N-times-over-a-rate shape — but it has no per-step floor/min-against-salvage comparison and no variable factor/life-derived rate, so it doesn't compose DDB, it only supplies the loop skeleton. Per docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md's own worked example (IRR/RATE: 'nominally composable but really an algorithm wearing a composable disguise' -> candidate, not composable-author), DDB's per-period min-floor + early-halt logic is genuine algorithmic complexity, not glue — same misclassification risk the amendment warns about, so it should enter as a candidate cell rather than be authored as composable-author.

entries.name: DISC
entries.description: Returns the discount rate for a security
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: days_between (partial: covers actual/360, actual/365 only); is_leap_year, is_valid_date, day_of_year, days_in_month as supporting date primitives — 30/360 US/EU and actual/actual basis conventions still need new cells
entries.repr: date-composition (day-count-convention cells) feeding a checked-int/f32 final ratio
entries.reason: DISC = (redemption - pr) / redemption * (B / DSM), where DSM (days from settlement to maturity) and B (days in year) are both computed under a caller-chosen basis (0=30/360 US, 1=actual/actual, 2=actual/360, 3=actual/365, 4=30/360 European). cell80 has `days_between` (docs/cell-index.md:136, a Rata-Die actual-calendar-day count) plus `is_leap_year`/`is_valid_date`/`day_of_year`/`days_in_month`, which cover the actual/360 and actual/365 bases directly (DSM = days_between, B = fixed 360/365), but the 30/360 US and 30/360 European bases need special day-of-month adjustment rules (not just a calendar day difference) and actual/actual needs a coupon-period-aware year length — none of that day-count-convention logic exists as a cell yet, matching the background note's day-count-convention gap almost exactly. This isn't host_only (no transcendental, no array-state — settlement/maturity/pr/redemption/basis are all fixed scalar fields) and it isn't composable-skip/author either, since the missing piece is genuine new arithmetic-on-dates logic, not glue over existing outputs. Once basis-specific DSM/B cells land, the final DISC ratio itself is a one-line composition with the existing checked-multiply/divide idiom (e.g. the mul_div_sat / discount-style shape already in money-bps).

entries.name: DOLLARDE
entries.description: Converts fractional dollar prices to decimal format
entries.repr: checked-int
entries.reason: No existing cell80 cell reads a decimal-digit-literal fractional part and rescales it by a denominator's digit count — that's DOLLARDE's actual algorithm (Excel: int(x) + (x-int(x))*10^digits(fraction)/fraction, digits = decimal-digit-count of fraction). cell80 already has the pieces `num_digits` (docs/cell-index.md:438, digit-count of fraction, e.g. num_digits(16)=2) and `pow_small` (docs/cell-index.md:446, 10^digits) plus `frac_add_whole` (cell-index.md:271, whole+num/den reassembly, gcd-reduced) for the final recombine step, but nothing in fractions/fixed-point/money-bps composes those into the actual digit-scaling formula — that glue is new logic, not a chain of existing outputs, so this isn't composable-skip/author, it's a real candidate. Best target is a checked-int signature that takes the fractional part already decomposed as an integer digit-literal (whole: u16, frac_digits: u16, fraction: u16) rather than a raw float, since DOLLARDE's semantics are inherently digit-literal (not a true binary value) and cell80 has no f32-parses-decimal-literal primitive to lean on; f32 is a plausible alternate tier (fsub/fmul/fdiv/round kernels exist per docs/real-valued-cells-amendment.md) but risks re-deriving decimal digits from a float rather than taking them as given. No transcendentals, no arrays, no day-count convention involved, so none of the host_only grounds apply; it's a small bounded arithmetic cell, not an algorithm-in-disguise (no iteration/convergence), so it clears candidate cleanly rather than tripping the reason-2 misclassification check.

entries.name: DOLLARFR
entries.description: Converts decimal dollar prices to fractional format
entries.repr: f32 (paired with a small checked-int digit-count/power-of-ten helper)
entries.reason: No existing cell80 cell does this, and nothing in docs/cell-index.md glues to it directly: DOLLARFR's algorithm is trunc(decimal) for the whole-dollar part, remainder = decimal - whole, numerator = round(remainder * fraction), digits = number of decimal digits in `fraction` (exactly `num_digits`'s counting-loop technique, cell80/cells/number-theory), then result = whole + numerator / 10^digits. That digit-count-driven divisor is the well-known Excel "gotcha" of DOLLARFR/DOLLARDE (fraction=16 -> divide by 100, fraction=128 -> divide by 1000) — genuine convention fragility, not a trivial one-hop composition. Crucially, the f32 primitives it would need (truncate, round-to-int, multiply, the int_to_f32 conversion) are dialect-level softfloat kernels, not standalone retrievable cells in cell-index.md — only composite application cells built ON them are searchable (lerp_f32, norm2_f32, clamp_f32, the physics f32 cells), and cells can't call each other per the pack's own documented constraint (see q_bilerp's summary). So there is nothing to compose FROM at the retrieval layer, which rules out composable-skip/composable-author and puts this squarely in candidate: a new f32-tier cell authored the same way lerp_f32/norm2_f32 were (direct softfloat kernel use), reusing num_digits' divide-until-zero loop for the digit-count step and frac_pow's repeated-multiply idiom for building 10^digits. Not host_only: no transcendental is needed (this is truncate/round/multiply/divide, an integer power-of-ten via bounded repeated multiply), no array-state field is needed (fixed 2-scalar-in/1-scalar-out signature), and it has no day-count-convention dependency at all (it's a pure decimal<->fraction price encoding, unrelated to calendar cells like day_of_week/days_between).

entries.name: DURATION
entries.description: Returns the annual duration of a security with periodic interest payments
entries.missing_capability: array-state fields (arbitrary-length coupon-period schedule), compounded by absent day-count-convention cells
entries.reason: DURATION(settlement, maturity, coupon, yld, frequency, basis) = Macaulay duration = sum_{i=1..n}[t_i * CF_i / (1+yld/freq)^t_i] / price, where n is the number of coupon periods between settlement and maturity — for real bonds (e.g. a 20-year semiannual note) that's dozens of periods derived at call time from the two dates, not a fixed small arity. CellHost's runner zeros a state cell's fields every run() and only round-trips named SCALAR fields (experiments/sliding-window-state-cells-findings.md) — it cannot hold or iterate over that variable-length cash-flow/date schedule, so this is the array-state-field gap by name, not a vague "too complex." It's also compounded by a real second gap: DURATION's basis parameter selects a day-count convention (actual/actual, 30/360 US/EU) to turn (maturity-settlement) into fractional periods, and per docs/cell-index.md's calendrical-checksum pack, only bare calendar primitives exist (day_of_week, day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date, is_weekday, is_weekend) — no convention logic. Note the exponentiation itself, (1+yld/freq)^t_i over an integer period count, is NOT a blocker — that's the frac_pow checked-repeated-multiply idiom already shipped (cell80/cells/fractions/frac_pow.rs); a fixed-small-arity variant (duration for exactly N named coupon-period fields) could plausibly dodge the array gap, but would still need a day-count-convention cell and wouldn't match Excel's actual open-ended settlement/maturity signature, so it classifies against that real signature.

entries.name: EFFECT
entries.description: Returns the effective annual interest rate
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: div_floor_u32 + compound_increase_by_bps
entries.reason: EFFECT(nominal_rate, npery) = (1 + nominal_rate/npery)^npery - 1 is exactly the integer-period compounding idiom cell80/cells/money-bps/compound_increase_by_bps.rs already ships (loop v += v*bps/10000 for `periods` iterations, checked/escalating): derive the per-period bps rate with div_floor_u32(nominal_bps, npery), run compound_increase_by_bps with value=10000 (bps base for 1.0) and periods=npery, then subtract 10000 from the result to get the effective-rate delta. No transcendental or array-state is needed (npery is a small integer period count, not a fractional exponent). This is the same shape the taxonomy's own worked table already calls out for PMT/FV/PV/NPV (docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 4) — a well-known, externally-named TVM function with real convention fragility (order of operations: divide-then-compound-then-subtract-1, easy to get subtly wrong by hand each time), so it clears reason 1 the same way that row does. It is not genuine complexity (reason 2) — it is simple glue over an already-shipped loop, not a new algorithm.

entries.name: FV
entries.description: Returns the future value of an investment
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: frac_pow (fractions pack) + compound_increase_by_bps (money-bps pack)
entries.reason: FV(rate, nper, pmt, [pv], [type]) is fixed-arity (never a variable-length schedule, so no array-state-field gap) and nper is an integer period count, so (1+rate)^nper is exactly the repeated-checked-multiply idiom cell80 already ships twice — frac_pow (raise a fraction to a whole-number power via repeated mul_checked_u32) and compound_increase_by_bps (loop the same rate over N periods); the PMT annuity-stream term is the same compounding sum, not a new algorithm class, so this stays glue rather than crossing into genuine-complexity/candidate the way IRR/RATE's Newton iteration does. It clears composable-author on reason 1 alone: FV is a well-known, externally-named atomic op (Excel compatibility) with fragile conventions worth encoding once — the cash-outflow-is-negative sign convention, the pv=0/type=0 omitted-argument defaults, and the rate==0 special-case branch are all easy to get subtly wrong re-deriving by hand each call site. docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 4 already pre-classifies PMT/FV/PV/NPV this exact way (composable-author, reason 1), distinguishing them from IRR/RATE (candidate, reason 2 misclassification flag).

entries.name: FVSCHEDULE
entries.description: Returns the future value of an initial principal after applying a series of compound interest rates
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: combined_bps_increase, increase_by_bps (fixed-arity 2-rate path only)
entries.missing_capability: array-state fields — FVSCHEDULE's second argument is Excel's "schedule", an arbitrary-length array of per-period interest rates applied sequentially (FV = principal * Π(1+rate_i)), not a fixed small set of scalars. CellHost's runner zeros a state cell's fields before every run() and only round-trips named SCALAR fields, never arrays, so this input shape can't cross the call boundary today (same gap as NPV/IRR/XNPV).
entries.reason: Excel's FVSCHEDULE applies a variable-length, per-period-varying rate schedule to a principal (distinct from compound_increase_by_bps, which loops the SAME rate for N periods — that's ordinary FV, not FVSCHEDULE). The per-step arithmetic itself is trivial checked multiplication (the frac_pow/compound_increase_by_bps idiom), so this isn't a transcendental or day-count gap; it's blocked purely because the "schedule" argument is an arbitrary-length array and array-state fields don't round-trip across CellHost's run() boundary yet. A fixed small-arity variant is a real, already-available path today: for exactly 2 rates, combined_bps_increase(bps1, bps2) (compose two different sequential bps rates into one equivalent rate) followed by increase_by_bps(principal, combined) reproduces FVSCHEDULE for a 2-entry schedule exactly, and nesting combined_bps_increase would extend to 3-4 fixed entries. But Excel's actual signature takes an arbitrary-length array, so against that real signature this is host_only on the array-state-field gap, not composable.

entries.name: INTRATE
entries.description: Returns the interest rate for a fully invested security
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: days_between, mul_div_sat (reused for the actual/360 and actual/365 sub-cases only)
entries.repr: checked-int (u32 ratio, bps-style) layered on a new date-composition day-count-convention primitive
entries.reason: INTRATE = (redemption - investment) * B / (investment * DIM), where DIM is days-between-in-basis and B is the basis year length; Excel's real signature takes a `basis` argument (0=30/360 US, 1=Actual/Actual, 2=Actual/360, 3=Actual/365, 4=30/360 European). cell80's calendar cells (`day_of_year`, `days_between`, `days_in_month`, `is_leap_year` — cell80/cells/calendrical-checksum/) only give raw Gregorian calendar-day differences, not day-count CONVENTIONS: two of the five bases (30/360 US, 30/360 European) need a synthetic 30-day-month day-count with end-of-month adjustment rules that doesn't exist as a cell at all, and Actual/Actual needs an actual-year-length rule, also absent. So while the actual/360 and actual/365 sub-cases are trivially composable today from days_between + a mul_div-style ratio (matching cell80/cells/checked-arithmetic/mul_div_sat.rs's shape), the function as Excel actually defines it is blocked on missing day-count-convention prerequisite cells, not on any transcendental or Newton-iteration complexity — per the coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment's guidance this is real candidate/prerequisite work, not host_only and not cleanly composable-skip.

entries.name: IPMT
entries.description: Returns the interest payment for an investment for a given period
entries.repr: checked-int / bps-rate (the compound_increase_by_bps + money-bps pack idiom: u32, escalate-on-overflow); f32 is a viable alternate tier if Finance80 wants Excel-literal decimal rates instead of bps
entries.reason: No PMT/FV/PV/NPV/IPMT/PPMT cell exists anywhere in the 653-cell library (checked money-bps, fractions, sequences, calendrical-checksum packs in docs/cell-index.md — nothing matches), so IPMT is not covered and there is no existing named financial cell to compose from. IPMT reduces to "rate times the loan balance remaining just before period `per`," but computing that balance needs the annuity payment sized first (an annuity-factor division built from (1+rate)^nper compounding), then the SAME compounding re-run to a second, shorter bound (per-1) for the running balance, plus type=0/type=1 and per==1 case branching for Excel's sign/timing convention — real multi-step algorithm work built on kin idioms already shipped (compound_increase_by_bps's repeated-bps-compounding loop, geometric_series_sum's summation, frac_pow's checked-repeated-multiply pattern), not 1-2 cell glue. Per the taxonomy amendment's own IRR/RATE precedent ("nominally composable but really an algorithm wearing a composable disguise" → candidate, not composable-author), IPMT lands the same way: rate/per/nper are given (no Newton iteration needed, so not host_only for transcendentals), all fields are fixed scalars (no array-state-field gap), and no date/day-count convention is involved (periods are abstract, not calendar dates) — so none of the host_only grounds apply either. It should enter a wave alongside PMT/FV (its natural prerequisites) rather than being authored solo, or IPMT/PPMT would each re-embed the same balance-compounding algorithm independently.

A fixed small-arity variant (e.g. IRR over exactly 3-6 named scalar cash-flow fields, Newton loop inlined) could dodge this and become a real f32/checked-int candidate later, but Excel's actual signature is arbitrary-length, so this row is classified against that.

entries.name: ISPMT
entries.description: Calculates the interest paid during a specific period of an investment
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: bps_of + frac_of_whole_floor
entries.reason: ISPMT(rate, per, nper, pv) = pv*rate*(per-nper)/nper is pure closed-form arithmetic — no compounding, no loop, no transcendental — so it's actually simpler than PMT/FV/PV/NPV (which the taxonomy doc's own worked-example table already calls composable-author). It composes cleanly from two existing checked cells: bps_of (pv*rate_bps/10000, giving the "full-principal" interest) then frac_of_whole_floor(n=nper-per, d=nper, whole=that product) to apply the straight-line remaining-term fraction. Reason 1 applies, not reason 2 (no genuine complexity here): ISPMT is a well-known, named Excel TVM function, and it carries real convention fragility — its straight-line-principal assumption is easy to conflate with IPMT's amortized/declining-balance formula, and the pv sign convention needs encoding once rather than re-derived by hand each time, exactly the "easy to get subtly wrong" case the taxonomy names as strengthening reason 1.

entries.name: MDURATION
entries.description: Returns the Macauley modified duration for a security with an assumed par value of $100
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: none — nearest related existing cells are money-bps's compound_increase_by_bps/compound_decrease_by_bps (single-rate N-period compounding loop idiom to reuse) and calendrical-checksum's days_between/day_of_year/is_leap_year (calendar-day primitives that a future day-count-convention cell would build on), but none of these compose directly into MDURATION
entries.repr: date-composition (coupon-period/day-count prerequisite) feeding an f32 discounted-cash-flow loop
entries.reason: Not covered — cell-index.md has no bond/duration/coupon cell in any pack (money-bps's 16 cells are all single-rate bps compounding/discount, not multi-period cash-flow duration; softfloat has only lerp_f32/norm2_f32; calendrical-checksum has day_of_week/day_of_year/days_between/days_in_month/is_leap_year/is_valid_date/is_weekday/is_weekend but no day-count CONVENTION cell). Neither piece exists: (a) is blocked on the day-count-convention gap named in the task background (real primitive prerequisite, not just calendar day differences — days_between/day_of_year don't encode 30/360 or actual/actual), and (b) is a genuine bounded loop with two running accumulators (sum and per-step discount factor via repeated multiply, the frac_pow/compound_increase_by_bps idiom but in f32 since yld/frequency is a real fraction) — not glue over 1-2 existing cells, so it fails composable-skip/composable-author and lands as candidate work per the amendment's IRR/RATE precedent (genuine algorithmic composition, not a disguised composable). It is not host_only under the stated ground rules: no transcendental is needed (integer-period compounding), and no arbitrary-length array input is needed (N is derived internally from dates, not passed in as a variable-length schedule) — so the array-state-field gap doesn't bite here the way it does for IRR/NPV. The real blocker is the day-count-convention prerequisite; MDURATION should wait behind that landing rather than being authored as one leaf cell today.

entries.name: MIRR
entries.description: Returns the internal rate of return where positive and negative cash flows are financed at different rates
entries.reason: Excel's MIRR takes an arbitrary-length values array (plus finance_rate/reinvest_rate) and must partition it into positive/negative flows, compound the positives at reinvest_rate, discount the negatives at finance_rate, then take the (n-1)th root of their ratio minus 1 — the arbitrary-length schedule is the exact case docs/cell-index.md confirms cell80 has no cells for at all (no npv/irr/pmt/fv/pv/rate cell exists anywhere in the 653-cell index; grepped for pmt/fv/pv/nper/annuity/"cash flow"/"present value"/"future value" with zero hits), and CellHost's runner zeros a state cell's fields before every run() and never round-trips arrays across the call boundary (experiments/sliding-window-state-cells-findings.md), so a variable-length cash-flow input cannot be represented today regardless of the rate-solving arithmetic. The final root-extraction step (n-1 th root of a ratio) is itself fine under the stated ground rules — it's a bounded Newton iteration parameterized by n, the same non-transcendental idiom isqrt_u32/bps_rate_over_2_periods already use for n=2 — so that alone would not block it. A fixed small-arity variant (e.g. MIRR for exactly 3-4 named scalar cash-flow fields) could in principle dodge the array gap, but it would still need wholly new FV/PV-style compounding-and-discounting logic that doesn't exist in the library today (this is new-authoring territory, not composition), so even that path is candidate/greenfield work, not something to build now — the row is classified against Excel's actual arbitrary-length signature, which is host_only today.

entries.name: NOMINAL
entries.description: Returns the annual nominal interest rate
entries.reason: NOMINAL = npery * ((1+effect_rate)^(1/npery) - 1) is the EFFECT-inverse and fundamentally needs a general Nth root (npery is any small positive integer — 1, 2, 4, 12, 52, 365 — not fixed at 2). cell80's only root primitives are square-root-only (`isqrt`, `isqrt_u32`, cell80/cells/money-bps/bps_rate_over_2_periods.rs which explicitly special-cases exactly 2 periods via isqrt and calls a general Nth root "unbuildable before isqrt_u32 landed" even for that fixed case). Extracting an Nth root for arbitrary npery is a genuine iterative algorithm (Newton-Raphson: x_{k+1} = x_k - (x_k^npery - c)/(npery*x_k^(npery-1)), pure add/mul/div, no transcendental needed) — the same 'arithmetic + bounded loop, not a transcendental' shape docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md's worked-example table already uses to file RATE/IRR as `candidate` rather than `composable-author` or `host_only`. This isn't glue over 1-2 existing cells (frac_pow only does integer-power forward compounding, not root extraction), so per the amendment's reason-2 self-check it belongs in `candidate`, not composable-anything. Target tier: f32 (shipped fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv are sufficient for the Newton loop) with a new general-N nth-root kernel plus the final npery* scale/subtract — logic beyond anything in fractions/, money-bps/, or softfloat/ today.

entries.name: NPER
entries.description: Returns the number of periods for an investment
entries.missing_capability: transcendentals — specifically ln (or a general fractional-exponent pow)
entries.reason: Excel's NPER solves for the exponent n in FV = PV*(1+rate)^n + PMT*(1+rate*type)*((1+rate)^n-1)/rate, whose closed form is nper = ln((pmt*(1+rate*type) - fv*rate)/(pmt*(1+rate*type) + pv*rate)) / ln(1+rate) — the unknown sits in the exponent itself, so this is a genuine logarithm, not a bounded loop. That's structurally unlike RATE/IRR (classified `candidate` in docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md's worked-example table) where the unknown sits in the polynomial's base and Newton's method can solve it with pure arithmetic; here Newton's own derivative step still needs ln(1+rate). cell80's closest existing cell, `bps_rate_over_2_periods` (money-bps pack), only manages this for exactly 2 periods via isqrt_u32's degree-2 bisection, and its own doc comment says recovering a rate over MORE than one period needs an Nth root that isn't buildable yet — NPER is the same gap one level worse (solving for the root/exponent itself, across an arbitrary and generally fractional period count). No ln/exp/pow-with-fractional-exponent cell exists anywhere in docs/cell-index.md (softfloat pack has only lerp_f32/norm2_f32; checked-arithmetic/fractions only have integer-exponent pow via frac_pow/pow_checked_u32, which require a known integer exponent, the opposite of what NPER needs).

entries.name: NPV
entries.description: Returns the net present value of an investment based on a series of periodic cash flows and a discount rate
entries.missing_capability: array-state fields — CellHost's runner only round-trips named scalar fields across a call boundary (resets state each run()), so an arbitrary-length list of independently-valued cash flows (Excel's value1..value254) cannot be passed in; this is distinct from the transcendentals gap and from day-count-convention gaps.
entries.reason: Excel's NPV(rate, value1, [value2], ..., [value254]) sums value_i/(1+rate)^i over an arbitrary-length list of periodic cash flows (i = 1..n, n up to 254) — the variable arity IS the function's defining behavior, distinguishing it from PMT/FV/PV which take a fixed handful of scalars. Cell80 has no array/buffer state across a call boundary today: CellHost's runner zeros a state cell's fields before every run() and only round-trips named SCALAR fields (experiments/sliding-window-state-cells-findings.md), and every existing compounding cell in cell-index.md — frac_pow (fractions pack), compound_increase_by_bps/compound_decrease_by_bps/compound_original_before_increase (money-bps pack) — takes `periods` as a plain scalar loop count over one repeated rate, never a per-period array of independently-valued cash flows. The per-term discounting itself is not the blocker: (1+rate)^i is exactly frac_pow's already-shipped repeated-multiply-with-overflow-escalation idiom, and no transcendental is needed (i is an integer count). The blocker is purely that Excel's real signature needs N independent scalar inputs for arbitrary N, which the harness cannot represent. A fixed small-arity variant (e.g. npv_3/npv_4 over exactly 3-6 named scalar cash-flow fields, composing frac_pow-style discounting + repeated add) would dodge the gap and could be candidate work later, but graded against Excel's actual arbitrary-length signature this is host_only today.

entries.name: ODDFPRICE
entries.description: Returns the price per $100 face value of a security with an odd first period
entries.missing_capability: transcendentals — ODDFPRICE discounts each quasi-coupon cash flow by (1+yld/freq)^(k-1+DSC/E), where DSC/E is a genuine fraction of a coupon period (that's what makes the first period "odd"); the exponent is non-integer, so this needs real pow(base, fractional exponent) = exp(x*ln(base)), not frac_pow's integer-exponent repeated-multiply idiom. Compounded by a second real gap: the DSC/E, A/E day-count fractions themselves depend on basis conventions (actual/actual, actual/360, 30/360 US/EU) that cell80 has no cells for today (only day_of_week/day_of_year/days_between/days_in_month/is_leap_year/is_valid_date/is_weekday/is_weekend exist in calendrical-checksum).
entries.reason: docs/cell-index.md has zero finance-pack cells at all (no PMT/PV/FV/NPV/RATE, no bond/coupon/redemption/settlement/basis vocabulary anywhere) — searched exhaustively across calendrical-checksum, checked-arithmetic, fractions, money-bps, percent, softfloat. Unlike RATE/IRR (candidate per the amendment's Part 4: Newton iteration over integer periods, no transcendental needed) or PMT/FV (composable-author via frac_pow's integer-exponent repeated multiply), ODDFPRICE's defining "odd period" feature forces a genuinely fractional exponent in the discount factor, which is a real pow/ln/exp requirement — not glue over existing cells, and not reachable by any bounded-loop trick. It also independently needs day-count-basis conventions that don't exist as cells. Both gaps are real prerequisites (not scalar-arity workarounds like the array-state-field IRR case), so this is host_only rather than candidate.

entries.name: PDURATION
entries.description: Returns the number of periods required by an investment to reach a specified value
entries.missing_capability: transcendentals — specifically natural logarithm (ln). rustz80/softfloat.rs-derived f32 kernels visible in cell-index.md (lerp_f32, norm2_f32) plus the isqrt_u32/q_sqrt family cover arithmetic, compare, round, convert, and integer square roots only; no ln/log/exp/pow-with-real-exponent kernel exists, and PDURATION's closed form needs exactly ln(fv/pv)/ln(1+rate).
entries.reason: PDURATION = (LN(fv) - LN(pv)) / LN(1+rate) — a continuous, generally non-integer period count, so the answer literally requires a natural-logarithm evaluation, not a bounded loop. Surveyed docs/cell-index.md: no ln/log/exp/pow-with-real-exponent cell exists anywhere (softfloat pack is only lerp_f32/norm2_f32, arithmetic-only); the isqrt family (isqrt_u32, q_sqrt, bps_rate_over_2_periods) covers square roots only, never a general root/log. frac_pow's repeated-multiply idiom (which covers PMT/FV/PV integer-period compounding) doesn't apply here since it needs a known integer exponent, and PDURATION is the inverse problem with a fractional answer. Unlike RATE/IRR (Newton's method over a fixed-arity polynomial for a fixed integer n — arithmetic + bounded loop, not transcendental), there's no iterative substitute that reproduces Excel's exact fractional-period value without an actual log kernel.

entries.name: PMT
entries.description: Returns the periodic payment for an annuity
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: frac_pow (FracPow::run) for the (1+rate)^n compounding-factor idiom (checked repeated multiply, same technique geometric_nth_checked_u32 uses) + f32 arithmetic (fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv, the shipped IEEE binary32 dialect tier that already backs lerp_f32/kinetic_energy_f32/etc.) for the surrounding pmt = rate*pv / (1 - (1+rate)^-n) algebra

entries.reason: grep of docs/cell-index.md finds no pmt/annuity/finance cell and no dedicated finance pack — not covered. It's technically composable: nper in Excel's PMT is an integer period count, so (1+rate)^nper is exactly the frac_pow/geometric_nth_checked_u32 checked-repeated-multiply idiom (no transcendental needed), and the rest is plain f32 add/sub/mul/div, all shipped, bit-identical primitives. Encoding those once as a tested cell is worth the retrieval-cost tax even though the arithmetic itself is glue of frac_pow-style compounding + f32 ops.

entries.name: PPMT
entries.description: Returns the payment on the principal for an investment for a given period
entries.repr: f32 (real IEEE binary32 tier) — rate/pv/fv/pmt are real currency/rate quantities, not naturally bps-quantized; per/nper are integer period counts driving bounded fmul loops, the same idiom cell80/cells/fractions/frac_pow.rs already ships (checked repeated multiply) just ported to f32.
entries.reason: Not covered — grep of docs/cell-index.md turns up no pmt/ipmt/ppmt/annuity/payment cell anywhere (money-bps's `compound_increase_by_bps` only compounds a single value forward at one rate/one horizon; it doesn't split a specific period's payment into interest vs principal). PPMT needs (1) a growth-factor loop (1+rate)^nper for the whole-loan annuity-payment formula, (2) a SECOND growth-factor loop (1+rate)^(per-1) to get the balance remaining at the start of period `per`, (3) the interest-portion formula off that balance, (4) ppmt = pmt - interest, plus a type(0/1) branch (ordinary annuity vs annuity-due) with a per==1-under-type=1 zero-interest edge case. That's genuine multi-step case analysis, not gluing 1-2 existing cells' outputs — per docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 2 reason 2's own warning, this is exactly the shape that "usually means it isn't glue-composable at all" (its own worked table files IRR/RATE this way for the same reason, and even PMT/FV/PV/NPV, which the amendment DOES pre-file as composable-author, are simpler — one growth-factor loop and one closed form, not two loops plus a period-split). Building blocks it would reuse once authored: `frac_pow`'s repeated-checked-multiply idiom (ported to f32) and the checked-arithmetic pack's add/sub/mul/div kernels, but the annuity-balance/period-split algorithm itself is new logic that doesn't exist yet at any layer.

entries.name: PRICE
entries.description: Returns the price per $100 face value of a security that pays periodic interest
entries.missing_capability: transcendentals — a real/fractional-exponent power in the discount factor (1+yld/freq)^(...+DSC/E), which is not integer compounding (frac_pow's repeated-multiply idiom doesn't apply since the exponent isn't a whole number) — AND day-count conventions — no basis-parameter (30/360 US/EU, act/act, act/360, act/365) or coupon-schedule date-stepping logic exists; only plain calendar-day primitives (day_of_week, day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year) are shipped.
entries.reason: PRICE's own formula — redemption/(1+yld/freq)^(N-1+DSC/E) + sum_k[100*(rate/freq)/(1+yld/freq)^(k-1+DSC/E)] - 100*(rate/freq)*(A/E) — raises (1+yld/freq) to a generically non-integer exponent (k-1+DSC/E, since settlement normally falls between coupon dates), which is a real power-with-fractional-exponent, not the integer-period compounding frac_pow already covers (cell80/cells/fractions/frac_pow.rs). Separately, DSC/E/A require a basis-parameter day-count convention (30/360 US/EU, act/act, act/360, act/365) and coupon-schedule date stepping (N coupon dates counted back from maturity by frequency) — cell80/cells/calendrical-checksum/ only ships day_of_week, day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date, is_weekday, is_weekend (docs/cell-index.md lines 134-143), none of which encode a day-count convention or coupon-period arithmetic. Both gaps are independently blocking.

entries.name: PRICEDISC
entries.description: Returns the price per $100 face value of a discounted security
entries.repr: date-composition (extends calendrical-checksum) + checked-int for the final scaling
entries.reason: No existing cell computes a day-count-basis-adjusted day fraction. docs/cell-index.md's calendrical-checksum pack (day_of_week, day_of_year, days_between, days_in_month, is_leap_year, is_valid_date, is_weekday, is_weekend) only gives raw calendar day counts/validity — none encode any of Excel's 5 day-count bases (0=30/360 US, 1=actual/actual, 2=actual/360, 3=actual/365, 4=30/360 European) that PRICEDISC's basis argument selects between. PRICEDISC = redemption * (1 - discount * DSM/B) where DSM (days settlement->maturity) and B (days in the basis year) are both basis-dependent; days_between alone cannot produce either. Per the day-count-conventions guidance, this is a real prerequisite gap, not just missing glue — so it's candidate work (author the basis primitives first), not composable-skip/author off today's library, and not host_only since nothing here is transcendental or needs array-state (fixed 4-5 scalar inputs: settlement date fields, maturity date fields, discount, redemption, basis). Once DSM/B exists, the price formula itself is a single multiply-divide-subtract, the same idiom as discount_percent/decrease_by_bps, so most of the new work is the day-count basis logic, not the pricing arithmetic.

entries.name: PRICEMAT
entries.description: Returns the price per $100 face value of a security that pays interest at maturity
entries.repr: date-composition (day-count basis convention) feeding f32 arithmetic for the price formula
entries.reason: PRICEMAT's core formula — price = (100 + (DIM/B)*rate*100) / (1 + (DSM/B)*yld) - (A/B)*rate*100 — is just a few multiplies/adds and one division (no iteration, no transcendental), so it's not host_only on the transcendentals ground, and all inputs (settlement/issue/maturity dates, rate, yld, basis) are fixed scalars, so it's not host_only on the array-state-fields ground either. But it fundamentally depends on the `basis` argument selecting one of five day-count CONVENTIONS (actual/actual, actual/360, actual/365, 30/360 US, 30/360 European) to compute DSM/DIM/A — and cell80's existing calendar cells (`day_of_week`, `day_of_year`, `days_between`, `days_in_month`, `is_leap_year`, `is_valid_date`, `is_weekday`, `is_weekend` in cell80/cells/calendrical-checksum/) only give calendar day counts and Gregorian validity, none of the 30/360 or actual/actual bond-convention day-count rules. No existing cell in docs/cell-index.md composes to this (checked money-bps/percent cells like decrease_by_bps, bps_of, frac_pow give the bps/fraction arithmetic idiom but nothing touches day-count basis). Per the coverage-map amendment's day-count guidance, this is real candidate work with a prerequisite, not a composable row and not host_only: first author the day-count-basis primitives (a small family of date-composition cells per basis code), then a PRICEMAT cell that composes those with f32 (or bps/fixed-point) rate/yield arithmetic for the final division.

entries.name: PV
entries.description: Returns the present value of an investment
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: compound_original_before_increase + geometric_series_sum
entries.reason: PV(rate, nper, pmt, [fv], [type]) is fixed-arity (5 scalar params, no cash-flow array), so unlike NPV/IRR it does NOT hit the array-state-field gap (CellHost never round-trips array fields across a call). It composes from two existing cells: compound_original_before_increase (money-bps pack) already does exactly PV's lump-sum term — reverse-of-compounding, discounting a final value back N periods via a repeated v = v*10000/(10000+bps) loop; and geometric_series_sum already does exactly PV's annuity term — the iterative sum of a geometric sequence with ratio (1+rate), which is the closed-form annuity growth factor ((1+rate)^nper-1)/rate. Both use integer-loop compounding over an INTEGER period count, not a transcendental (matching frac_pow/geometric_nth_checked_u32's established repeated-multiply idiom), so no dialect gap blocks this. This matches docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md's own Part 4 worked example, which lists PMT/FV/PV/NPV together as composable-author under reason 1. entries.name: RECEIVED
entries.description: Returns the amount received at maturity for a fully invested security
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: days_between (cell80/cells/calendrical-checksum/) gives raw calendar days but not a basis-weighted year fraction; no existing cell encodes 30/360 US/EU or actual/actual day-count conventions

entries.name: RRI
entries.description: Returns an equivalent interest rate for the growth of an investment
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: bps_rate_over_2_periods (N=2 special case that RRI generalizes); frac_pow / geometric_nth_checked_u32 / is_square_u32 (checked-power-evaluation and binary-search idioms the new cell would reuse)

entries.name: SLN
entries.description: Returns the straight-line depreciation of an asset for one period
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: sub_checked_u32 (cost - salvage) -> round_div_checked_u32 (result / life); f32 tier equivalent is fsub -> fdiv if fractional cost/salvage/life are needed

entries.description: Returns the sum-of-years' digits depreciation of an asset for a specified period

entries.name: VDB
entries.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset for a specified or partial period by using a declining balance method
entries.reason: No depreciation cells exist yet in cell80 (grep of docs/cell-index.md finds no DDB/SLN/SYD/VDB — the only adjacent cell is `compound_decrease_by_bps`, which loops a *fixed* bps rate for N whole periods, with no switch-to-straight-line logic and no partial-period support). It isn't host_only either: nothing here needs a transcendental (factor is applied via repeated multiply, the frac_pow idiom already shipped) and there's no array/variable-length input or day-count convention involved — only fixed scalar args (cost, salvage, life, start_period, end_period, factor, no_switch).

entries.name: XIRR
entries.description: Returns the internal rate of return for a schedule of cash flows that is not necessarily periodic
entries.missing_capability: transcendentals (fractional-exponent compounding) AND array-state fields — two independent, both-fatal gaps

entries.name: YIELDDISC
entries.description: Returns the annual yield for a discounted security; for example, a Treasury bill
entries.repr: date-composition (day-count/DSM prerequisite) + f32 (final yield ratio arithmetic)
